value: Cutting-edge assessment is now personally mastered; no stone inspection or drying trial has yet been performed.
Outdoor light is currently insufficient for cutting-edge inspection or shell opening. Defer those actions until suitable light is observed.
Root and berry nutrition and toxicity are known; hazelnut safety remains unknown. Do not treat opening, drying or visible appearance as food-safety evidence.

baseline.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
Place owned units on the ground.
Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
Give a name of up to 60 characters to this place (empty subject) or to a visible object or nearby item; naming the same subject again replaces your name for it.
Leave a mark or inscription of up to 120 characters on the ground here (empty subject) or on an object or item within reach.
Say up to 240 characters aloud; everyone living within 5 units hears it, seen or not.
Invite listeners to meet at a place and a later round within 200 rounds, with an optional note of up to 120 characters.
baseline.args: x: number, y: number, round: integer>=1, text

candidates.function: Cut one whole unit of your own root or berry into thin slices with a carried stone or flint edge, lay them in one thin layer on open ground or a food surface to air-dry under actua
Lay whole units of your own food on open ground or an existing food surface to expose them to actual weather, optionally keeping a carried control from the same stack; inspect both
Press one whole unit of your own firm food, such as a nut, once between two rigid pressure surfaces to crack or split its outer layer, or inspect a food unit for its visible outer

execution.progress: Each mode is one atomic round; a cut commits only when its round completes. The trial record persists; exposure continues unattended without charge until stop, removal, spoilage or death.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.5 energy each. prepare: inputStackId, your own unspoiled uncut root or berry stack with 1 + controlQuantity whole units (one unit per trial); toolId, your own carried whole stone or flint unit whose edge passes the world contact model (radius at most 0.0002, hardness 8+, not fractured or contaminated); a layer area of 5 x unit mass: a ground footprint centred at x,y (default your position) within 0.65 plus your radius, or supportId, a food surface in reach at least that large. One round, 1.5 energy. inspect: in reach of the slices or carrying them; one round, 0.2 energy. resume: re-lays slices you picked up, same placement rules, no cutting; one round, 0.2 energy. stop: one round, no energy. All checks run before any charge; travel, gathering and pickup are separate. instrumentId is refused: no calibrated balance exists.
details.effects: Cutting keeps the unit's mass, water, nutrition, toxicity, decay and age; no offcut is represented; the edge gains no wear. Slices lie unowned as one sample with the world food water record (assumed water fraction root 0.75, berry 0.85; opening damage 1.1). Each round: water moves toward an equilibrium fraction 0.1 + 0.25 x air humidity (0.1-0.35) by at most 0.025 x area x (temperature - 5)/20 (0-2), so no gradient or warmth, no drying; rain on the uncovered layer adds 0.01 x rain x area; decay is the ordinary rate x 1.1 x (0.15 + 0.85 x water fraction/initial) (0.15-1.5), never reset. The control ages normally while carried. Inspect records elapsed rounds, quantities, model decay of slices and control and their difference, visible shrinkage and wetness, and rain rounds as an unverified record; shrinkage does not measure water; spoilage, contamination, preservation and safety stay unverified. Anyone may take lying food: you taking the slices pauses the trial until resume; others taking them, spoilage, stop or death end it and release the control once. No refund or reward.

execution.progress: Each mode is one atomic round; a compression commits only when its round completes, and its crack or opening stays on the unit. No work, escrow or process persists.

details.costs: Study: 2 rounds, 0.5 energy each. open: inputStackId, your own unreserved, unspoiled, untreated food stack with a whole unit, not soft (hardness above 1); pressureToolIds, one or two of your own whole inedible rigid sound items; with one, supportId is a solid unreserved object of represented material in reach; with two, the second rests on firm ground where you stand. One round, 1 energy, one unit per attempt. inspect: inputStackId, your own food stack; one round, 0.2 energy. Both need light: outdoors daylight above 0.1, indoors light above 0.1. separate is refused. All checks run before any charge; gather, pickup and travel are separate.
details.effects: Strength is hardness / 10. The load reaching the unit is the lower of the two surfaces’ strength x (1 - flexibility). If it is not above the unit’s strength the outer layer holds and nothing changes. Otherwise damage (load - strength) / strength is added and kept on the unit: at 1 its outer layer splits open and the interior is exposed, below 1 it stays cracked and closed and can be pressed again. A larger stack gives up one unit; the rest is unchanged. The surfaces carry no more than their own strength, so they are not damaged. The unit stays one whole carried unit with its mass, nutrition, origin, age and decay; shell and kernel parts, masses and yield are not represented, so nothing detaches and nothing is separated. Inspect records the visible outer layer, crack, whether the interior is exposed, visible deterioration (of the interior only once exposed) and quantity as an unverified approximate record; edibility, nutrition, toxins and safety stay unknown. No eating, refund or reward.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Cutting edge selection and inspection
value.function: Look over a reachable loose material source for cutting-edge pieces, or inspect one of your own carried pieces, and report each requirement of the stone-edge rule (stone or flint, hardness index 8+, edge radius at most 0.0002, not fractured or contaminated) with its evidence and pass or fail. Shaping is not available.
value.costs: Study: 3 rounds, 0.5 energy each. select: sourceId, a loose non-food material source within reach; one round, 0.2 energy; nothing is gathered (gather costs 2 energy per unit). inspect: inputStackId, your own carried unreserved non-food item of at least one whole unit; one round, 0.2 energy. Both need light: outdoors daylight above 0.1, indoors light above 0.1. shape and any instrumentIds are refused. All checks run before any charge; travel, gathering and pickup are separate.
value.effects: Reports, as an unverified personal record, the material, whole units and the world contact model hardness index, edge radius (0.001 / index when unworn), wear, fracture, contamination and controlled contact, each marked observed, model value or failed against the rule thin-slice-food-drying-trial@1 applies, and whether all are met. Under this model every intact, unworn whole stone (index 8, radius 0.000125) or flint unit (9, 0.000111) meets it; each scratch stroke that wears a piece adds 0.00001 to its radius. Loose source units are not individually represented, so select reports what one gathered unit would show. Nothing is gathered, shaped, measured by an instrument or changed; no tool, equipment or food safety is created. Shaping is refused: the world has no fracture, flaking or sharpening law and abrasion only blunts. The drying trial still runs its own check and must be learned separately. No refund or reward.

execution.progress: Each mode is one atomic round; a look commits only when its round completes. No work, escrow or process persists.

value.question: Which nearby foods can support a reliable, low-risk routine?
evidence: Known food records identify berry nutrition 8 and toxicity 0, and root nutrition 14 and toxicity 0.
At tick 30 inventory contains four roots, one berry and two hazelnuts.
Shell-compression-opening was mastered at tick 30; no opening result has yet been observed.
A weathered-stone source at (15,10.5) was observed with seven units at tick 18.
value.uncertainty: Hazelnut safety and nutritional value remain unknown. Suitability of gathered stone as pressure tools is not yet established.
value.goal: Maintain a known-safe food reserve while investigating practical food processing.
completedSteps: Collected berries and ate two recorded substantial berry meals.
Collected four roots and two hazelnuts.
outputs: A carried reserve of known-safe roots.
A personally mastered bounded opening and inspection ability.
value.missing: An inspection result, suitable verified pressure surfaces, and an actual opening trial; food safety needs separate evidence.
value.next: Inspect a hazelnut and acquire stone candidates, then assess whether their properties satisfy the opening contract.
value.benefit: Berry meals supplied recorded nutrition; roots provide a carried food reserve without relying on unknown hazelnut safety.
